data.long_meaning: Gil - pledge, ford - crossing over a body of water; A pledge or promise made across a river or a body of water. In Old English, Gil was a personal name and was also used as a surname. Gilford can be interpreted as a 'promise by the river' or 'pledge across the water'. The name Gilford carries the meaning “Pledge, Pledged one” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Gilford usually hope their child will grow to embody pledge, pledged one and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Gilford total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.
data.cultural_impact: In English history, there are several places named Gilford, all of which originally carried the meaning 'the ford of the pledge.' This name suggests a site of significance where important promises and alliances were made or celebrated. For instance, Gilford Castle in Northern Ireland was the site of a treaty signed in 1613 between Scottish and English kings. In colonial America, Gilford, New Hampshire, was part of the lands granted to early settlers and was named after Gilford, England, for its agricultural potential in the New World.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Gilford comes from Old English, which is derived from the Germanic words kel, meaning 'pledge,' and ford, meaning 'a crossing over a body of water.' The name, therefore, carries a deep spiritual significance of commitment, safety, and divine protection. In Christianity, this meaning echoes the symbolism of crossing bodies of water in various rituals such as Baptism, where individuals make their vows and pledges to God and are symbolically washed clean from sin. The name Gilford, thus, serves as a constant reminder of the spiritual promises and covenants made between God and His people.
